To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the outbreak in Jiangxi in China in 2009 was caused by CV- A24 variant (AHC) and that the classification of CV-A 24v isolated after year 2010 worldwide based on phylogenetic tree using VP1 region was consistent with the one based on the 2C region.

the outbreak was most likely caused by CV-A- 24v and that the classification of CV-A- 14v isolated after 2009 was based on the VP 1 region and was almost consistent with the classification based on the 30C region.

coxsackieviruses A24v were isolated in 2010 from patients with acute hemorrhagic conjuntivitis (AHD) in Jiangxi, which were divided into two lineages, and the classification of coxsackievirs A24v based on VP1 region is almost consistent with that of 3C region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular identification and phylogenetic analysis of CV-A24 causing AHC outbreak in Jiangxi in China.
the molecular identification and phylogenetic analyses of CV-A24 causing the outbreak of AHC in Jiangxi in the year 2010.
the molecular characterization and evolutionary analysis of CV-A24 in Jiangxi, providing useful data for further studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CV-A24 variant was the causative agent of AHC outbreaks in Jiangxi, 2010, which belonged to GIV, and could be divided into two transmission lineages.
CV-A24 is the most important causative agent of AHC outbreaks in Jiangxi, and the outbreak was caused mainly by CV-A24 strains belonging to GIV-C5.
CV-A24 was the cause of the outbreak of AHC in Jiangxi in the year 2010.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CV-A24V is still circulating in the world.
the classification based on the VP4 region was the most accurate, followed by that based on the VP2 region.
the CV-A24v outbreak in Jiangxi in China in 2009 was caused by two lineages (A and B) belonging to GIV-C5, which were similar to CV-A24v in other parts of the world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CV-A24 is still a major cause of AHC outbreaks in the world, especially in Asia.

the 3C gene is a more suitable target for phylogenetic analysis and molecular surveillance of CV-A24 than the VP1 gene, because of the greater number of nucleotide substitutions and more variable nucleotide positions in the 3C than in the VP1 gene.
the phylogenetic trees constructed based on the 1C and VP1 genes can be used to classify and trace CV-A24v worldwide.
